result:
The `@latest` alias now resolves to the highest version number of the model, so it matches the `/latest` path form in every case, including when that version is archived. The new tests pass on the SQL store. The file-store tests I added are skipped repo-wide ("FileStore is no longer supported"), so the file-store change was never actually run.

**Cause:** both registry stores answered `@latest` with the first entry of `get_latest_versions(name)`. That call returns one latest version per stage, in no particular order, so the first entry is often not the newest. The path form takes the highest version from the same list (`mlflow/store/artifact/utils/models.py:48`).

**Changes:**
- **`mlflow/store/model_registry/sqlalchemy_store.py`**: `get_model_version_by_alias` now returns the highest version across all stages instead of the first one.
- **`mlflow/store/model_registry/file_store.py`**: the same fix. It also now raises a "Latest version not found" `MlflowException` when the model has no versions, where it used to crash with a bare `StopIteration`.
- **Tests:** the two tests already staged in `tests/store/model_registry/test_sqlalchemy_store.py` cover a model spread across several stages and the case where an older version is moved to Production. I added the same two tests to `tests/store/model_registry/test_file_store.py`.

Models without stages, such as prompts, keep their current behaviour: all their versions sit in one stage, so the list has a single entry. The alias- and latest-related tests in both files give 18 passed and 8 skipped.
